questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Two sides of a job market
questions.learningObjective: distinguish the vocabulary an employer uses from the vocabulary an applicant uses
questions.stem: A company has posted a notice about a vacancy, and a candidate has sent in an application for the same post. Which pairing of the two Chinese terms with the two sides of that exchange is right?

options.text: 招聘 names the employer's side of advertising a vacancy, and 求职 names the side of seeking a job
求职 names the employer advertising a vacancy, and 招聘 names the side that will be hired
options.misconception: swaps the two roles, when 招聘 is built around the post being offered and 求职 around the work being wanted

options.text: 招聘 names the applicant applying for the post, and 求职 names the employer naming who is hired
options.misconception: reads 招聘 from the point of view of the person who applies, ignoring that the character 招 invites or calls for

options.text: 招聘 and 求职 both name the moment of being hired, so the two differ only in how formal the notice sounds
options.misconception: collapses two different stages into one, when one term covers advertising and the other covers looking

questions.explanation: The two terms divide the exchange in the same place the real process divides it. 招聘 is the employer calling for someone to fill a post, so it belongs to the notice, the sign outside the building, and the page on a job site; 求职 is somebody looking for work, so it belongs to the person reading that notice and writing an application. A learner who keeps the two apart can predict which word belongs in which document without needing to memorise them, because the first character carries most of the work: 招 invites or summons, 寻 seeks. The distractors each fail in a different way. B swaps the sides, and swapping them is easy because both words are commonly seen in job advertisements, which are written for the employer and read by the applicant. C is the same swap told from the other end. D is the error that costs the most, because it treats the words as two ways of saying the same finished fact, when one of them belongs to a stage before anyone has been chosen and the other to a stage before anyone has been found. A third term is worth knowing in the same family: 应聘 is what the applicant does when responding to a specific offer, which is a later moment than 求职.
questions.hint: Ask which side of the exchange each word belongs to, and read the first character of each as an action.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: What a vacancy notice selects for attention
questions.learningObjective: infer the reading a vacancy notice asks of its evidence
questions.stem: A posted vacancy lists the years of experience required, the exact salary range, and the hours, but says nothing about what the work involves day to day. Which reading of that notice is best supported by the evidence it actually gives?

options.text: The notice is written to let an applicant judge whether they meet stated conditions, so it states conditions and leaves the work to be asked about
The notice is incomplete, because a vacancy notice that omits the daily work cannot legally be published at all
options.misconception: invents a rule about publication, when what a notice must contain is not the question the evidence can answer

options.text: The notice is meant to discourage applicants, because a post with a salary range attached attracts too many replies to be manageable
options.misconception: reads a screening function into a detail, when publishing pay is ordinary rather than a deterrent

options.text: The notice is confident about the post, because a writer who omits the daily work has clearly already decided what the work is
options.misconception: treats silence as certainty, when an omission shows only that the writer did not put that information in this document

questions.explanation: A notice is a selection from a description, and the same kind of selection a headline makes: the writer chooses what a reader needs in order to decide whether to go further, and leaves the rest to be asked about. Here the three items given are all testable in seconds against a background that has none of them, so putting them in does the work of a filter, and the daily work is left out because it takes a conversation to state. That is not a defect in the document; it is what the document is for. The distractors each read more into the omission than the evidence supports. B imports a legal requirement the notice itself gives no sign of, and it is the kind of confident rule a learner meets in advice about advertisements rather than in the text. C assigns a motive that the salary range actually works against, since publishing a figure is a way of attracting applicants who can check, not of turning them away. D is the most interesting option, because it is close to a real observation: a firm that can state its conditions precisely usually does know the work. But knowing the work and writing it down are separate acts, and the evidence in front of the reader shows only the second. A reader should be able to say what the notice is optimising for, and here it is a cheap first comparison rather than a full description.
questions.hint: Ask which items in the notice a stranger could check in ten seconds, and what kind of document that selection suits.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: order the stages a search actually follows into a working sequence
questions.stem: Five stages of one job search have been listed out of order by a class. Only one sequence is the order in which the work is actually done. Which sequence is it?

options.text: 先看招聘广告，挑出合适的一家公司 / 准备材料，把简历和求职信一起寄出去 / 收到通知后去面试 / 再经过一次复试 / 拿到录用通知以后再去签劳动合同
准备材料，把简历和求职信一起寄出去 / 先看招聘广告，挑出合适的一家公司 / 收到通知后去面试 / 拿到录用通知以后再去签劳动合同 / 再经过一次复试
先看招聘广告，挑出合适的一家公司 / 收到通知后去面试 / 准备材料，把简历和求职信一起寄出去 / 再经过一次复试 / 拿到录用通知以后再去签劳动合同
先看招聘广告，挑出合适的一家公司 / 准备材料，把简历和求职信一起寄出去 / 再经过一次复试 / 收到通知后去面试 / 拿到录用通知以后再去签劳动合同

questions.explanation: The workable order is the first one, and each stage sits where a search would otherwise waste effort. Reading the notices comes first because it decides what the rest is for: an application written before anyone has read a notice has to guess at the post, and a guess is what a covering letter is least able to hide. Materials come second for the same reason, since there is no point preparing a document for a post you have not chosen. The first interview comes third, because it is the first moment anybody can assess a candidate, and the second round comes fourth, since a second round is by definition a second look and cannot precede the first. Signing the contract is last, and this is the stage candidates most often get wrong in their expectations: an offer is not yet a contract, and a person who treats the offer as the end of the process stops reading the document that follows. The second option sends the application before the notices are read. The third has the candidate turning up for an interview with nothing sent, which is a sequence the process cannot run at all. The fourth is the subtler error, because it puts the second round before the first, and a second round without a first round is not a harder test but a different job.
questions.hint: Ask which stage decides what the rest of the work is for, and which document a person still has to read after an offer arrives.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: identify which items belong in an application packet and which do not
questions.stem: An applicant is assembling what to send for a post and has written a list. Which pairing of a document with the purpose it actually serves in the packet is correct?

options.text: 简历 gives the facts of education and work history, and 求职信 gives the argument for why the applicant fits this post
简历 gives the argument for why the applicant fits, and 求职信 repeats the dates and titles already listed there
options.misconception: swaps the two documents, when a sheet of dates and a letter of argument are not the same kind of object

options.text: 简历 replaces the letter entirely, because a complete sheet of history leaves a letter with nothing to add
options.misconception: believes a record of facts speaks for itself, when facts do not choose themselves as reasons

options.text: 求职信 is a formality that must be sent first, and 简历 may follow later if the employer asks for it
options.misconception: invents an order the practice does not require, when the two normally travel together in one packet

questions.explanation: The two documents do different kinds of work, and the division of labour is the same one a school report and a covering note make. 简历 is a record: dates, places, titles, qualifications, laid out so that a reader can check a claim against a period. It is written to be skimmed, which is why it is short and why it leads with the facts a reader needs in order to decide whether to keep reading. 求职信 is an argument: it names the post, says why this applicant's experience is relevant to it, and says what the applicant is offering. Neither can do the other's job, and the reason is worth stating in terms of what each is for. A record cannot argue, because its entries are not selected to persuade; a letter cannot record, because it has no space and no way of showing the shape of a career. The distractors each collapse the two. B is the reversal that is most tempting, because both documents mention the same job, and a candidate who has not seen a real packet easily assumes the letter is the important one and the sheet is the paperwork. C is the belief that a strong record needs no advocacy, which fails on jobs where several candidates meet the stated conditions equally well. D invents a protocol that does not exist, and a candidate who waits to be asked for a sheet loses weeks.
questions.hint: Ask which document is written to be skimmed and which is written to persuade, and what each cannot do.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Word order when handing over documents
questions.learningObjective: apply the disposal construction to an act of handing something to somebody
questions.stem: A speaker wants to say that she gave her resume to the recruiter and put a copy on the desk. In which sentence does the object come before the verb, as this construction requires, in both clauses?

options.text: 我把简历交给招聘的人，又把复印件放在桌上。
我交给招聘的人简历，又放在桌上复印件。
options.misconception: keeps the verb in front of its object, which is the order the construction is being used to avoid

options.text: 我给了招聘的人我的简历，又把复印件放在桌上。
options.misconception: switches to a verb with a double object, so the two hands of the exchange take different grammatical routes

options.text: 我把简历给了招聘的人，又放了在桌上复印件。
options.misconception: puts the aspect particle before the final noun, when the particle has to follow the whole verb phrase

questions.explanation: The disposal construction exists to move an object forward, and it can only do that if the object comes before the verb, so the shape to look for is: 把, then the object, then the verb, then any particle. In the keyed sentence both halves follow that shape, which is what lets one sentence carry two acts that both involve handling something. The particle 着 in the second half is what makes 放在 describe an end state rather than an action, and it is what lets the two halves share one action. The distractors each fail the same test in a different way, and the test is worth memorising precisely because it is mechanical. B keeps verb-before-object order, which is the order the unmarked sentence uses; wrapping it in 把 without moving anything produces a construction that says nothing the plain sentence did not. C is the option a learner is most likely to produce, because 给 with two objects takes them in a fixed order and the second object is not introduced by 把, so the sentence is grammatical and yet the two halves are built on different principles, which is exactly what makes it feel wrong when read aloud. D puts the particle in a position the language does not use, since the aspect particle belongs after the verb phrase and not in the middle of a noun phrase.
questions.hint: Ask where the object sits in each half of the sentence, and whether the aspect particle follows the whole verb phrase.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: judge which section a resume should put first and why
questions.stem: Two applicants send the same kind of sheet. One puts a name and a way of being contacted at the top, then work history. The other puts a personal statement at the top and the contact details on the last page. Which judgement about the two sheets is fairest?

options.text: The first sheet matches what a reader needs first, since a reader who cannot contact the applicant cannot act on anything else in the document
The second sheet is better, because a personal statement is always what a reader decides on before reading a single date
options.misconception: assumes a fixed reading order that is not in the evidence, since where a reader looks first depends on what the reader came for

options.text: Both sheets are wrong, because a resume that gives a name at the top is a letter and not a record
options.misconception: confuses the two document types, when a sheet of history conventionally carries a name and a letter is a separate object

options.text: The difference is a matter of taste only, since every reader is known to work through both sheets from top to bottom
options.misconception: claims a single fixed reading habit, when a skimming reader takes headings and the top of the page by design

questions.explanation: A resume leads with what a reader needs in order to take the next step, which is a way of reaching the person, and everything else on the sheet is conditional on that. The reason is not politeness and it is not a rule about formality: a document that puts an uncontactable applicant first has arranged itself for a reader who will stop reading before the contact details arrive. This is the same principle as putting the conclusion of an argument first when the reader is short of time, and it is worth naming as a principle because it generalises. The distractors each smuggle in an unsupported certainty. B treats a personal statement as decisive, and while a statement can be decisive it cannot be decisive for a reader who has not yet been given the means to act, and it also assumes a fixed order of reading. C confuses a resume with a letter, and the confusion is understandable only if the reader has never seen both documents in a packet. D is the one worth pushing back on hardest, because it sounds like modesty and is actually a claim: readers skim, they take headings, and a sheet that requires a top-to-bottom reading is a sheet that will be skimmed anyway.
questions.hint: Ask what a reader has to be able to do after the first few lines, and what that implies about the order.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: judge a register choice in a written record of work history
questions.stem: One sheet of work history records a post as 干了三年, and another records the same three years as 任职三年. Which account of the difference is the useful one?

options.text: The two carry different registers, and a written record uses the neutral form because the reader has no relationship to the writer
The two mean different lengths of time, so the first records three full years and the second records three years of anything
options.misconception: reads a register difference as a difference in the fact, when both phrases point at the same period

options.text: The first is the more impressive form, because 干 is the verb an employer prefers to hear from a candidate
options.misconception: ranks the forms by force rather than by register, when a spoken verb is chosen for its casualness

options.text: Both are wrong, because a written record of a post has to use 做过 and no other verb can report a duration
options.misconception: invents a single obligatory verb, when several verbs report a duration and the choice is about register

questions.explanation: The difference between the two phrases is register, and register in a resume is not decoration: it tells the reader what relationship the document imagines between them. 干了三年 is what a person says out loud about their own working life, to somebody they already know, and it carries a plainness that is entirely appropriate in speech. 任职三年 is the same fact in the impersonal form a document uses, where the writer is not a participant in the conversation but the source of a record. A learner who can feel this difference will avoid the opposite error too, which is putting a spoken phrase into a document and making the document sound like a voice rather than a file. The distractors each misdescribe the difference. B is the tempting one because a lexical difference usually is a difference in meaning, and checking whether it is here is the whole skill: both phrases point at the same span of time, so the difference must be elsewhere. C ranks by force, which is a plausible guess about a verb like 干, and it is wrong in an instructive way, since the plainness of that verb is not a strength a reader is rewarding. D invents an obligatory verb and so forbids a phrase that is entirely standard on a resume.
questions.hint: Ask who is speaking in each phrase, and what relationship to the reader the document imagines.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: The claim a covering letter makes
questions.learningObjective: state the claim a letter of application has to make
questions.stem: A candidate writes a covering letter that lists every date in the resume, adds nothing about the post, and closes with a request to be considered. Which statement about that letter is accurate?

options.text: The letter has not made its claim, because a claim of fit is not the same as a copy of the record already given
The letter has made its claim, because thoroughness is what persuades a reader and a complete record persuades best
options.misconception: mistakes completeness for argument, when a reader who already has the record gains nothing from a second copy

options.text: The letter has not made its claim, because a claim of fit has to be stated only in the first sentence or not at all
options.misconception: invents a position rule, when what matters is that the claim is made rather than where it sits

options.text: The letter has made its claim, because asking to be considered is itself a statement that the applicant is the right person
options.misconception: treats the request as the argument, when a request is what a reader is being asked for and not a reason

questions.explanation: A covering letter exists to make one claim that the resume cannot: that this applicant is the person for this post. Everything the letter says should be a reason for believing that, and the reason has to connect something in the record to something the employer needs. A letter that lists the same dates in a new arrangement has made no claim at all, because a record does not select itself, and selection is the whole work of a claim. This is worth stating as a general principle, because it also explains why a covering letter for a post in a different field can be short: the record is the same, the selection is different, and only the selection is new. The distractors each mistake a feature of the document for its argument. B is the error that rewards diligence in exactly the wrong place, and it is common among candidates who believe that a fuller letter must be a better letter. C invents a position rule, and the rule it invents is a common coaching tip rather than a fact about the language, since a claim made in the third sentence is still a claim. D confuses the request with the reasoning, and it is worth noticing that D's letter would be perfectly persuasive if the reader already assumed the fit.
questions.hint: Ask what the letter says that the resume does not, and whether a record selects itself.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: explain what the honorific form of the company's name marks in a letter
questions.stem: A letter to a company opens 尊敬的贵公司负责人 and later 贵公司. What is the honorific contributing, and what would be lost if it were dropped?

options.text: It marks the reader as the party the letter is being presented to, and dropping it makes the letter read as a message about the firm rather than to it
It marks the letter as official, so a letter without it would carry the same request with less force behind it
options.misconception: reads the honorific as force, when it marks the addressee rather than the strength of the ask

options.text: It marks respect for a particular individual inside the firm, so a letter addressed to no one in particular should not use it
options.misconception: narrows the form to a person, when the construction takes a company or an office as readily as a name

options.text: It marks the applicant as the outsider, so a letter that dropped it would be read as coming from somebody inside the firm
options.misconception: inverts what the form signals, since the distance it creates is the distance the applicant is asking to be given

questions.explanation: 贵 in front of a company is an address form, and what it does is place the firm on the receiving end of the letter rather than the subject of it. A letter can be about a company, and then a plain 公司 is exactly right; a letter that is addressed to a company needs to mark it as the party being written to, and that is the work 贵 does. Removing it does not make the letter rude, and it is worth saying that plainly, because candidates often believe otherwise and then avoid a form they do not need. What is lost is the framing: without the honorific the sentences read as statements about the firm rather than requests made to it. The distractors each assign the form a job it is not doing. B treats the marker as force, which is the reading that produces the wrong advice of using the form to make a weak request stronger. C narrows it to an individual, and the construction in fact takes 公司 and 负责人 and a department with equal ease. D gets the direction backwards, and it is the most revealing error, because the form exists to establish that the writer is outside and the reader is inside, which is the position an applicant actually occupies.
questions.hint: Ask whether the company is the subject of the letter or the party the letter is written to.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: explain what the softening form contributes to an interview question
questions.stem: An interviewer asks 请介绍一下你自己 rather than 请介绍你自己. What has the added softening form done to the request?

options.text: It has marked the request as a short, ordinary act, which lowers the sense of command without changing what is being asked for
It has made the request smaller in scope, so the interviewer is now asking only for a summary rather than an introduction
options.misconception: reads the form as a limit on the content, when it changes the force of the asking and not the size of the answer

options.text: It has marked the question as informal, so the interviewer no longer expects the answer to be treated seriously
options.misconception: infers seriousness from register, when a plain form is used for serious questions as a matter of course

options.text: It has turned the sentence into a request for permission, so the candidate now needs an answer before giving one
options.misconception: reads the softener as a question about whether to speak, when the question mark is doing that work if anything

questions.explanation: The added form belongs to a small class of softeners that mark a single, short, ordinary act, and the effect is on the force of the asking rather than on the content of the request. Both sentences ask for an introduction; the softened one asks as though it were a small, ordinary thing to ask, which matters in an interview precisely because the person asking is in the stronger position. This is worth learning as a general pattern rather than as a fact about this one question, because the same form appears in requests to repeat something, to write something down, and to look at something, and in each case it lowers the imposition without changing the meaning. The distractors each attribute something the form does not carry. B is the most natural error, because a softener really does make something smaller in some senses, and the question is which thing is smaller: the force of the ask, not the length of the answer expected. C is a mistake worth naming as a habit, because seriousness attaches to the situation and not to the form a sentence happens to take. D is the confusion the softening form is most often blamed for, when what makes a sentence a request is the modal and the phrasing of the request, not the short form.
questions.hint: Ask what stays the same in the two sentences and what has changed, and separate the asking from what is asked for.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: diagnose why a familiar answer to a weaknesses question defeats its own purpose
questions.stem: Asked 你的缺点是什么, a candidate answers 我太追求完美了, and the interviewer's expression does not change. Which reading of that exchange is best supported?

options.text: The answer names a strength as a weakness, which is a move the question is set up to detect, so the candidate has not answered the question at all
The answer is too short, so the candidate should add a second weakness to balance the one already given
options.misconception: treats the problem as one of length, when the difficulty is the kind of thing that was named

options.text: The answer is honest in the way the question intends, since every careful worker does care too much about quality
options.misconception: accepts the claim at face value, when the question asks for something that could actually cost the candidate

options.text: The answer is a refusal, since describing a strength is the only way to avoid volunteering something an employer could use against the candidate
options.misconception: reads a dodge as strategy, when the cost of the dodge is higher than the cost of the answer

questions.explanation: The question is a piece of assessment, and it works because it asks for something the candidate would rather keep. An answer that converts the request into praise has therefore not answered it: the candidate has demonstrated that a question with a known trap in it can be passed over rather than met, which is itself the information the interviewer is collecting. A useful answer to this question names something real, states briefly what it costs, and says what is being done about it, and the third part is what turns a confession into a plan. The distractors each misread what went wrong. B is the error that arrives from a genuine concern, since a one-sentence answer to a question about a weakness is thin, and the answer is not made better by the addition the option recommends. C is the mistake worth naming most carefully, because the underlying claim is not false at all: many careful workers do care more about quality than is convenient. The point is that a fact being true does not make it an answer, and a candidate who is being honest about wanting to do well has said nothing about a difficulty. D is a clever reading with a fatal cost, since protecting against one question is a poor trade when the interviewer has noticed the manoeuvre.
questions.hint: Ask what the question is designed to find out, and whether the answer supplied any of it.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: choose between the polite and the plain pronoun for a person higher in rank
questions.stem: A new employee has to ask a department head for a decision. Which opening is the one that matches the default polite register for that pair of people?

options.text: 王经理, 您好, 我想请教您一个事情, 不知道您现在方不方便。
老王, 嗨, 我想问你一个事儿, 你现在有空儿吗。
options.misconception: assumes the casual form is friendly rather than a different relationship, when it names the two people as equals

options.text: 王经理, 你好, 我想咨询你一个事情, 不知道你现在方不方便。
options.misconception: keeps the job title right but the pronoun wrong, and a title does not by itself supply the politeness the pronoun carries

options.text: 王经理您好, 请问贵公司的人事部在哪个楼层, 麻烦您指一下路。
options.misconception: uses every polite form correctly but asks a question the writer cannot know is the one the reader works on

questions.explanation: The polite form 您 is the default for a person higher in rank, and it is not a courtesy extra: it is how the sentence says who the two speakers are. The keyed sentence uses it twice, once in the greeting and once in the request, which is what a learner should notice, because the greeting alone is not enough when the body of the sentence drops back to the plain form. A job title is a different device; it names the post rather than the relationship, and it is entirely possible to address somebody by title and then speak to them as an equal, which is option C. The distractors each represent a real option with a real cost. B is not wrong Chinese at all, and it is the right register between colleagues who are close, but the two forms in it name the relationship as one of equals, which is not the position a new employee is writing from. C keeps the title and loses the pronoun, and this is the commonest error precisely because the title feels protective. D is the instructive one: every form in it is correct, and the sentence is still a bad one, because politeness in the wrong place is a way of avoiding the thing that has to be said.
questions.hint: Ask which forms in the sentence establish the relationship, and whether the title alone establishes it.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: A message that breaks the register
questions.learningObjective: locate the line in a workplace message that fails on register rather than on facts
questions.stem: A message to a department head says 喂, 这事你看着办吧, 反正我这边没问题, 到时候再说, 拜拜. Every fact in it is true. Which statement about the message is the soundest?

options.text: Nothing in it is inaccurate, and the fault is that the register names the two people as equals and closes the exchange before the decision is made
The closing is the fault, because ending a message with a spoken sign-off is never acceptable in writing to a superior
options.misconception: fixates on the least consequential line, when the register problem runs through the whole message

options.text: The message is unusable, because a message to a superior has to begin by naming the request in the first line
options.misconception: invents a formatting rule, when a request can appear anywhere provided the register supports it

options.text: The message is correct for a colleague, so the only change needed is the name at the top
options.misconception: believes the register sits in one replaceable slot rather than being spread across every line

questions.explanation: The register of a message is not a property of one line but of the whole, and this message is the clearest available demonstration of that. The greeting treats the reader as a peer rather than a superior, the request 看着办吧 hands over a decision without giving the material a decision needs, the 到时候再说 defers the substance to nobody in particular, and the sign-off closes a conversation that has not opened one. Every claim in the message is true, which is exactly the point: accuracy and fitness are different properties, and a message can be entirely accurate and entirely unusable. The distractors each locate the fault too narrowly, which is the general error this item is built to catch. B singles out the sign-off, when the sign-off is a symptom. C invents a structural rule that does not exist. D is the most instructive, because it treats register as a slot that can be swapped, and a writer who believes that will produce messages that open politely and then drift back into the casual voice three lines later, which is the commonest failure in real workplace writing.
questions.hint: Go through the message line by line and ask at each point who the two people are being treated as.

options.misconception: invents an unpaid stage, when the person is employed and paid from the first day of the period

options.text: The period delays the start of the contract, so nothing binds either side until the trial has been passed
options.misconception: puts the period before the employment rather than inside it, when the contract is already in force

options.text: The period sets the standard of work, so an employee who meets it during the trial is guaranteed a promotion afterwards
options.misconception: reads a performance standard as a promise of advancement, which the clause says nothing about

C puts the trial before the employment, which would make the period meaningless, since the point of a trial is to assess someone in the job. The clause on working hours and leave, which fixes when the employee must be available
The clause on social insurance, which requires contributions to be made for the employee as well as the salary
The font the contract is printed in, which is chosen by the office and binds nobody to anything at all
options.misconception: confuses a property of the document with a term inside it, which is the error the question is built to catch

questions.explanation: A clause is a term that imposes an obligation on one party or both, and the four keyed items each do that in a way a reader can act on. The post determines what the employee must do, and it is the clause most often left vague and most often relied on later. Confidentiality restricts disclosure, which is a real restriction on the employee and a real protection for the employer, and it is worth reading carefully because a clause drawn too widely can restrict more than the employer intended. Hours and leave fix the availability the employee owes, which is where the difference between a full-time post and anything else shows up in writing. Social insurance is a clause about the employer's own duty, and it is the one a candidate has the least reason to expect and the most reason to read, because a contribution owed is money that does not reach the employee. options.misconception: treats an open end as a permanent guarantee, when the whole purpose of the category is to govern how it may end

options.text: The fixed term is the better one for the employee, because a date certain is easier to plan for than an open arrangement
options.misconception: judges a category by convenience rather than by the notice it requires, which is where the two actually differ

options.text: The two descriptions name the same arrangement written at different levels of formality by different offices
options.misconception: reads a legal distinction as a stylistic one, when the distinction is exactly what a reader needs

An open-ended term has no end date, and it does not follow from that the relationship can never be broken; what follows is that breaking it requires a longer notice, which is the substance of the category. questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: explain why an advertisement asks about conditions rather than a figure alone
questions.stem: Explain in your own words why an advertisement asks about 待遇 rather than about 工资 alone, and say what a candidate goes on not knowing if the broader question is never put.

answer.exemplar: The two words ask for different sized objects, and the reason the broader one is used is that a figure is one component of what a candidate is deciding about. 工资 names the pay, which is a single number that arrives monthly and can be compared to another single number without any further information. 待遇 names the conditions of the post taken together, and it does so because the conditions are what the single number cannot show: how much leave the post carries, whether insurance and a pension are contributed, what the hours are, how the working year is divided. Those items are not small in aggregate, and the point about them is not that they are usually generous but that they are invisible from the figure, so a candidate who is only ever shown a figure is being asked to decide on the one component they can see. A second reason is that the broader word is not cold. Asking for a number carries an edge that asking for conditions does not, and an employer who wants a conversation about the post rather than a comparison of figures has a word ready for it. What a candidate goes on not knowing is the more useful half of the answer. If the question is never put, the untested assumptions fill the space, and they are almost always generous: most people assume the insurance is there, that the leave is the same as at the last workplace, and that the hours will be negotiable. The first of those is the one that costs most, because an item nobody asked about is an item nobody has checked, and it is discovered at the point where it cannot be changed. So the practical rule that follows is to treat any component of the package that nobody has stated as unknown rather than as probable, and to ask in the vocabulary of conditions rather than in the vocabulary of pay, since a question about pay cannot be answered with an answer about conditions.

questions.explanation: The exemplar is marked correct for treating 待遇 as a category rather than a synonym, for naming the specific components that the figure cannot show, and for the point that unasked items become assumptions rather than absences. A response that says the broader word is simply warmer has described the tone without explaining why the question is asked.
questions.hint: Ask what a figure cannot show, and what fills the space when a component is never mentioned.

questions.learningObjective: read a pay offer for the register it uses and what it declines to say
questions.stem: An offer reads 薪资待遇面议, 试用期三个月, 表现良好者可考虑转正. Which reading of the three clauses is the fairest, and which of them tells the reader something definite?

options.misconception: reads a conditional possibility as a commitment, which is the reading that would cost the reader most

options.text: The three clauses are a refusal, since a firm that does not publish a figure is telling the applicant not to apply
options.misconception: reads an unanswered question as a rejection, when the number is a matter for discussion in many posts

options.text: The three clauses are a trick, since 表现良好者 has no stated standard attached to it and therefore cannot be checked by anybody
options.misconception: jumps from an unstated standard to bad faith, when an unstated standard is ordinary and checkable in practice

C mistakes an unanswered question for a rejection, and a candidate who believes it will talk themselves out of posts they should be applying for. D is the sharpest observation and the wrong conclusion, since a standard that is not written down is still applied, and the absence of a number is not evidence of an intention to deceive.
questions.hint: Read the three clauses separately and ask which one tells the reader nothing definite.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: choose the construction that names a repeating interval rather than a weekday
questions.stem: A shift runs on and off in turn and a colleague must attend on alternate days. Which construction names that pattern?

options.text: 每隔一天上班, and it says every other day by counting the days between appearances
每周三上班, and it says every third day by counting the days between appearances
options.misconception: confuses a named weekday with an interval, when 每周三 fixes the day inside the week

options.text: 每天三小时上班, and it says every third day by counting the hours spent working
options.misconception: reads a duration as a frequency, when the number after 每天 counts hours and not days

options.text: 每三天一次上班, and it says every other day by counting the days between appearances
options.misconception: uses a real interval phrase and attaches the wrong meaning to it, since every three days is a three-day gap and not an alternation

questions.explanation: The language keeps intervals and named days in separate constructions, and putting the two together is the commonest mistake in timetables. An interval is expressed by counting the gap, which is what 每隔 does: 间隔 names the space between two appearances, so 每隔一天 means every other day. A named weekday is expressed by naming it, so 每周三 means every Wednesday, which is a fixed day of the week and not a two-day cycle at all. The distinction is easy to hold once it is stated as a rule about what is being counted: in one the unit is the gap, in the other it is the position in the week. The distractors each fail on that count. B is the swap that matters most, because a schedule that says a weekday is a completely different schedule, and someone relying on it will turn up on the wrong day. C reads a frequency phrase as a duration phrase, and it is a real trap because 每天 does appear in it and the number has moved. D is the subtler one because the phrase is a genuine interval phrase and only the reading is wrong: a three-day gap is a three-day gap, and translating it as an alternation is the same error as B in a different costume.
questions.hint: Decide whether the schedule fixes a day of the week or counts the gap between appearances.

questions.topic: Saying the span of a working day

上班时间是从早上九点开始, 下午六点就结束, 中午有一个小时的吃饭时间。

questions.learningObjective: distinguish the words a workplace uses for a rostered shift from the word for staying on the premises
questions.stem: A notice says 夜班, and another says 值夜. Which statement about the two is correct?

夜班 and 值夜 are two names for the same arrangement, since both are used for any work done after dark

options.misconception: invents a distinction of choice, which is a matter of the arrangement rather than of the word

questions.topic: The reason given in a safety rule

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: explain what a stronger prohibition removes and what it costs to ignore the difference
questions.stem: Explain in your own words how 严禁 differs from 不要 in what each one permits, and say what a reader gives up by treating the two as two styles of the same notice.

answer.exemplar: The two forms differ in how much they leave open, and the difference is easy to see in use even though both are translated as a simple negative. 严禁 marks a prohibition with nothing left to negotiate: it is the form a notice uses when the writer does not want a reader looking for a case in which the rule does not apply, and its implication is that no exception is available from the person reading it. 不要 is a negative instruction, and in ordinary conversation it is softer than the emphatic form, because a speaker who says 不要 has left the listener room to find a reason why the particular case is different. In a workplace the two sit closer together than that, since a rule addressed to everybody in a room with a hazard in it is read as allowing no exceptions whichever form it takes, and so the practical gap narrows. What remains is the amount of room the words offer, and the direction of the difference is the part worth holding on to: the emphatic form removes it and the plain form leaves some. A reader who treats the two as styles rather than as different amounts loses something specific. The first thing is the ability to recognise a rule that was written absolutely, which tells the reader something about the seriousness the writer intended and about the consequences that follow. The second is the ability to hear a shift: a workplace that moves from one form to the other has changed its mind about the matter, and a reader trained to hear style in that position will not notice the change at all. The third is the habit of asking for the exception in the right tone, because a request that a rule permits is made differently from a request against one. So the correction is not to use the emphatic form everywhere, which is a real and common overcorrection and it makes a speaker sound aggressive rather than careful. It is to keep the two apart so that a writer can choose the amount of room they mean, and a reader can hear which one they were given.

A response that says 严禁 is stronger has made the right observation and stopped one step short of what it is for.
questions.hint: Ask how much each form leaves a reader room for, and what a reader loses by hearing style in that position.

questions.learningObjective: weigh what a signed agreement settles and what it leaves to the individual

An individual starting salary is a number that belongs to a particular appointment, made at a particular moment, and the agreement does not contain it. This is a general point about how a collective document works rather than a detail about this one, and it is worth stating as a principle: a collective agreement fixes the frame, and individual appointments fill in positions inside that frame. questions.topic: The first stage of a dispute
questions.learningObjective: order the ways a workplace disagreement can be taken up
questions.stem: A worker has not yet been paid for three months of work. What is the sequence of steps available, in the order a disagreement like this normally travels?

仲裁 first, since a court will not look at a dispute that has not already been decided by an arbitrator
options.misconception: puts the formal step first, when the sequence begins with the two parties and their own representatives

options.text: A case in court, then 调解, then 协商, since the other steps exist only to delay a hearing
options.misconception: reverses the order and reads the sequence as obstruction, when each step exists to decide the matter

options.text: A complaint to the police, since unpaid wages are a matter the police rather than the parties must resolve
options.misconception: sends the dispute to the wrong body, because a wage claim belongs to a process built for employment terms

questions.explanation: The sequence runs from the two parties outwards, and every step is a place where the matter can be settled before the next one is needed. 协商 is negotiation between the employer and the worker or their representatives, and it is where most disputes are resolved, because a worker who is owed money and an employer who can pay it often have a shared interest in not going further. 调解 puts a neutral party alongside both, which is worth having when the parties cannot talk to each other but the gap is not deep. 仲裁 is a formal decision by an arbitrator, and for most employment disputes a court will not proceed until that step has been used, which is why the third place is not a choice between going further and stopping. B puts the formal step first, which confuses the most decisive step with the first one. C reverses the sequence and assigns it a motive, and that motive is the reason workers distrust the middle steps, so it is worth taking seriously as a fear rather than as a reading. D sends a wage claim to a body that has no jurisdiction over employment terms.
questions.hint: Ask which step involves only the two parties, and which step a court expects to have been used.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: select the considerations that bear on whether to begin a formal stage
questions.stem: A worker has settled the substance of a wage claim privately and is weighing whether to go on to arbitration. Four of the five considerations below are ones a careful worker should weigh. Which four?

options.text: Whether anything is still in dispute, since a stage that decides nothing has been paid for nothing
Whether the written record supports the claim, since an arbitrator works from documents and not from memory
What beginning will cost in time, which is usually the largest cost and the one least often counted
Whether the settlement was written down, since an agreement nobody recorded is the one most often disputed later
What an acquaintance of the worker thinks the outcome would be, which is a view worth having and is not a consideration
options.misconception: treats an opinion from outside the arrangement as one of the factors, when it carries no information about the case

questions.explanation: The four considerations in the keyed set share a property worth naming, which is that each is inside the worker's own control or inside the record. Whether anything is still in dispute is the first question, because a formal stage exists to decide something and a matter already settled privately has nothing to hand it; starting one does not confirm the settlement, it reopens it. The written record is the second, and it is the one most often skipped: a proceeding runs on documents, and a worker who cannot produce a record of hours, payments, or agreements will be arguing without evidence whatever the merits. Time is the third, and it is usually the largest cost because a formal stage runs in months while the wages are already overdue, so the honest comparison is between the amount claimed and the period it is tied up. Whether the settlement was written down is the fourth, and it protects a thing that has already been given up: an unrecorded agreement is the one most often denied afterwards. The fifth consideration is the one to reject, and it is rejected for a reason worth stating rather than for being unreliable. An opinion is not worthless, but it carries no information about the case, and a decision made on it is a decision made on somebody else's confidence rather than on the record.
questions.hint: Ask which of the five the worker can check without asking anybody else, and which one can be proved from a document.

options.text: Move the person to a different post, so the condition becomes irrelevant to the work the person is now doing
options.misconception: substitutes a change of job for a change of arrangement, which answers a different problem

options.text: Shorten the working day, so the person spends fewer hours exposed to the condition than before
options.misconception: assumes hours are the barrier, when the barrier is the task itself and hours would not remove it

In this case the job is not the obstacle and neither is the person: the obstacle is a physical feature of the task, so the accommodation is a change to how that task is carried out, such as a platform or a reassignment of that part of the work. The wording matters more than it first appears, because the alternative readings all change the job rather than the arrangement around it, and each of those is a different remedy for a different problem. Lowering the standard is what a support scheme does when a person cannot meet the requirement; moving post is what happens when the post itself is the barrier; shortening the day is what happens when duration is the barrier. questions.learningObjective: explain why length of service is a weak criterion on its own

It is unfair because it favours older workers, and age is never relevant to any work at all

options.text: It is unfair because it is easy to check, and a criterion that takes a minute to apply cannot be a real one
options.misconception: treats ease of application as evidence of emptiness, when several real criteria are equally easy to state

options.text: It is unfair because other employers use performance instead, and one employer cannot depart from what others do
options.misconception: reasons from what competitors do, which is a habit of mind rather than an argument about the post

C treats ease of checking as evidence of emptiness, and it would rule out almost every clause in a contract. D reasons from what competitors do, which is the habit a learner most needs to unlearn in a study of work.

questions.learningObjective: judge which sentence is usable as written feedback
questions.stem: A review document contains 你工作不够努力 and 三个月里你提交的报告有两次迟交。 Which of the two is the sentence a reader can act on, and why?

The first, because a general judgement about effort is a fair summary of three months of observation in a sentence

options.text: Neither, because written feedback is never about one person's work, and a review belongs only in a spoken conversation
options.misconception: invents a rule about the medium, since a written record is a normal part of a review

options.text: Both equally, because a reader can act on a general judgement as easily as on a specific one
options.misconception: denies the difference the whole discipline of feedback rests on

C invents a rule about the medium, and it is worth knowing that a written record is normally wanted precisely so that a conversation about it has something to point at. D is the denial of the distinction the item is built on.
questions.hint: Ask which sentence a reader could check against their own record, and what a reader would do differently next week.

questions.learningObjective: identify what a review conversation is conventionally built to do
questions.stem: A manager has scheduled a review conversation with one member of staff. What is that conversation conventionally built to produce?

options.text: A warning, because an unsatisfactory performance cannot be discussed anywhere else

options.text: A signature, since the point of a written record is to have something the employee has formally accepted

questions.learningObjective: distinguish an ordinary ending of employment from an exception to the notice rule

The two clauses cancel each other out, since a document that allows an exception cannot also state a rule
options.misconception: reads a rule and its exception as a contradiction, which is the ordinary structure of every set of terms

options.text: The second clause is the stronger and invalidates the first, since immediate termination is always available to an employer
options.misconception: turns a defined exception into a general power, which is how a clause becomes a threat

options.text: The two clauses describe the same thing, since thirty days written notice and immediate termination are two ways of saying the contract may end

questions.hint: Ask which clause sets the normal course and which names the case that does not follow it.

questions.learningObjective: explain why procedure carries weight in a dismissal

C is the belief that a reason is self-validating, and it is exactly what makes a claim unchallengeable. D reduces the whole thing to filing, which is the flattest version and the one a reader is most likely to arrive with after seeing a lot of paperwork in a workplace.

questions.learningObjective: read a sentence about an ending for the stance it takes

C measures neutrality by brevity, which is a plausible-sounding rule with no basis. D gets the direction of blame backwards, and it is the error a reader is most likely to make when meeting the word 辞职 for the first time.

questions.learningObjective: explain what a notice period protects on each side
questions.stem: A contract asks for one month's notice in writing from an employee who wishes to leave. What does the month protect?

options.text: Both sides, because the employer has a month in which to find cover and the employee has a month of pay in which to look

The employee gets an interval that is paid, during which they are still employed and still earning, which is worth something because the alternative to a month's notice is a month's work with no income. The clause is also a fairness device in a weaker sense: it gives both parties a chance to arrange matters rather than be surprised, and an arrangement made in advance is better than an arrangement forced by one side's urgency. The distractors each make the period one-sided or optional. B is the most common of the errors, because an employee's notice period is indeed paid and it is easy to read a payment as a cost rather than as part of the arrangement. C treats a clause as a formality, which is a claim about enforceability that a reader has no standing to make. D assumes the employer can fill the post at no cost, which is the assumption the clause exists to correct.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: diagnose a failed first conversation and choose an escalation that preserves the relationship
questions.stem: Stage one: two colleagues have disagreed in front of the team, a manager stepped in and told them both to sort it out between themselves, and nothing has changed for a fortnight. Diagnose why the arrangement the manager chose cannot resolve it. Stage two: say what the disagreement needs before the next conversation, and why that has to come before anybody is asked to decide who is right.

answer.exemplar: Stage one. The arrangement the manager chose puts the responsibility for the disagreement back onto the two people who are in it, which is the right instinct and the wrong instrument. A disagreement that has already happened in front of others is not only a disagreement about the work; it is a disagreement about standing, and two people who have just been told to resolve it privately are being asked to do something impossible in public terms, because any settlement they reach looks like a capitulation by whoever concedes first. The manager has also removed the only thing that made progress possible, which is the presence of a third person with no stake in the outcome, and a fortnight of nothing is what that absence produces. So the diagnosis is not that either of them is unwilling, which is what the manager assumed; it is that the dispute needs a place to be settled that neither of them controls. Stage two. What the disagreement needs before anybody decides anything is a statement of the actual point of dispute, in terms that are checkable. In most cases of this shape the visible row is about a decision and the real one is about a standard that was never written down, and a conversation between the two parties cannot settle that, because each is arguing from a standard only they hold. Once the standard is on the table the next step becomes obvious and mechanical: the manager supplies the missing standard, the two parties apply it to the decision, and the disagreement either dissolves or turns out to be about something else entirely. The reason this has to come first is that a decision about who is right taken before it is settled produces a winner and not a resolution, and a winner in a standing dispute leaves the dispute standing.

questions.explanation: The pairing tests a diagnosis and a remedy, and it is marked on whether the diagnosis finds the missing third party rather than the missing willingness, and whether the remedy puts a checkable standard on the table before anybody adjudicates. questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: explain what a record of a decision has to contain to be useful afterwards
questions.stem: A meeting ends after agreeing to change the release date, and the minutes record only 经过讨论, 大家同意调整时间. Explain in your own words what the record is missing, and state what a later reader would need in order to act on it.

answer.exemplar: The record is missing everything that makes the agreement actionable, and the reason is a grammatical one: the two sentences name a process and a conclusion without naming the content of either. 经过讨论 is an adverbial phrase that says a discussion happened, and it could stand in front of any verb; it says nothing about what was discussed. 大家同意调整时间 says that an agreement was reached about adjusting the time, and 调整 names an act without saying which time, or what it is adjusted to, or by how much, or from when to when. So the minutes tell a later reader that something was decided and nothing about what. A usable record needs three things, and the middle one is the one people leave out. It needs the content: the new date, written out rather than referred to. It needs the shape of the decision, which in this case is what the group has and has not agreed on, because a group that agreed to explore something and a group that agreed to a date have made very different commitments, and only one of them can be acted on. And it needs ownership: who is doing it and by when, since an agreement with no owner is a wish. The reason this matters more than it first appears is that the minutes are the only place these three things are written down at all. A decision made in a room exists for about ten minutes in the memory of the people who were there, and every later disagreement about what was agreed is settled by the record rather than by memory, which is why a record that states a conclusion without content settles nothing and starts the argument again.

questions.explanation: The exemplar is marked correct for identifying the gap as grammatical rather than merely terse, since the recorded sentences name a process and a conclusion but no content, and for naming ownership and the scope of the agreement as the two things usually omitted. A response that says the minutes are too brief has noticed the symptom; a response that says the verb is vague has found the cause.
questions.hint: Ask what 调整调整的是哪个时间, and who is responsible for carrying the agreement out.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: A delay notice that does not work
questions.learningObjective: diagnose why a delay notice fails and rewrite the part that carries the information
questions.stem: Stage one: a notice reads 因为最近事情比较多, 所以我们的进度可能要延后一段时间, 抱歉, 希望理解. Diagnose which single piece of information a reader cannot get from it. Stage two: say what the sentence has to supply, and why supplying it costs the writer something.

answer.exemplar: Stage one. The notice is fluent, apologetic and almost entirely uninformative, and the reason is structural. Because is a conjunction that makes the second clause depend on the first, and 最近事情比较多 is a statement about the writer rather than about the work, so everything after 因为 is presented as a consequence of the writer's circumstances. Then the actual event is described in the vaguest available language: 要 says it is still possible, 延后 says a date moves without saying to when, and 一段时间 gives no scale at all, since in Chinese usage that phrase covers anything from two days to two years. The single missing piece is therefore the new date. A reader who has the notice knows that something is late and knows that the writer is sorry, and cannot plan a single thing: not a dependant, not a supplier, not a colleague whose work was waiting. Stage two. The sentence has to supply the new date, and it should supply it in the first clause rather than at the end, because the reader's first need is the number and everything else is commentary on it. A workable version names the original date, names the new one, and says in one clause what has caused the gap, using 因为 to attach the reason to the work rather than to the writer's mood. It is worth noticing why supplying this costs the writer something, because that is what makes the item more than a writing exercise. A new date is a commitment, and a writer with no cause to report is better off writing 进度可能延后一段时间, which is vague enough to be true whatever happens next. Vagueness is therefore a defensive move and not simply carelessness, and the honest diagnosis is that the writer has not finished diagnosing, and no amount of rewriting substitutes for finishing the diagnosis. That is the general lesson: politeness is not the missing ingredient. A reader who has been told nothing that was not already obvious has not been treated politely, and the fact that the notice sounds considerate is exactly what makes it useless.

questions.hint: Ask what a reader cannot plan, and whether the reason given is about the work or about the writer.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: explain what a budget does and does not guarantee
questions.stem: Explain in your own words what a budget commits an organisation to and what it merely forecasts, and why a household that treats a balanced budget as a promise will be disappointed.

answer.exemplar: A budget is a plan expressed in money, and it is committed and forecast in different places, and the difference between the two is what makes it worth studying. A budget commits an organisation to the part it can control in advance: the posts it has decided to fill, the equipment it has decided to buy, the contracts it has signed. Those are decisions already taken, and a figure attached to them is a record of a decision rather than a prediction about a world. The rest is a forecast: travel, catering, repairs, anything whose size depends on what the year brings. Both kinds of number are written the same way, in a column, under a heading, which is why the difference is invisible on the page and has to be supplied by the reader. That is the whole problem a household runs into. A household that has balanced its budget has proved one thing, which is that the income it expected covers the spending it listed, and that is a statement about two lists rather than about a year. Three ordinary things break it. Prices move, so the same shop costs more in a different month. Unexpected expenses arrive, and a budget without a reserve has assumed they will not. And the household's own behaviour responds to what is left, which is the point most often missed: a budget that leaves nothing spare is a budget that creates pressure, and pressure is spent. The reserve is therefore not a saving; it is the part of the plan that absorbs the gap between a forecast and the year, and a household that has none has not planned more tightly, it has planned more hopefully. The general form of the lesson is that a balanced budget is a statement about arithmetic and not about security, and that a plan which is entirely forecast and entirely commitment has failed at one of the two jobs a plan has.

A response that says budgets are only plans has made a weaker claim than the one available here.
questions.hint: Ask which numbers are records of decisions already taken and which are predictions, and what a plan with nothing spare does to behaviour.

questions.explanation: A usable household budget has to do three jobs, and the four headings cover them. It has to spread the costs that do not recur across the year, since a family that budgets only for this month and not for the annual bill is budgeting for a month in which it will be short. It has to count all the income, and this is the heading people leave out most often: a budget that records a salary and omits a second source has a total that is too small, and every other figure in it is then measured against the wrong number. And it has to hold a reserve, which is the least optional of the four and the one most often skipped, because a reserve feels like an accounting entry rather than an expense. Its function is not saving and it is not a windfall; it is the money that pays for the thing nobody predicted, and a plan without one converts a surprise into a crisis by removing any way of meeting it. questions.topic: The limits of a price comparison

questions.stem: Two shoppers compare a bag of rice and a bag of noodles, work out which is cheaper per kilo, and the one who bought the rice is pleased. Explain in your own words what that comparison assumes, and what it leaves out.

answer.exemplar: The comparison is arithmetically correct and it has quietly changed the question being asked, and that is what is worth noticing. Per kilo is a measure of goods, so the comparison silently treats two things as interchangeable in the only respect it can measure: how much of them there is. A kilo of rice and a kilo of noodles are not two answers to the same question, because they will not be eaten in the same number of meals, they will not keep for the same time, and they will not be used in the same dish. A bag bought in error is not a cheaper bag; it is money spent and then thrown away, and the per-kilo calculation is blind to the throwing away, which is exactly where the real difference between the two purchases appears. So the first assumption is that a kilo is a unit of need rather than only a unit of weight, and it is not. The second assumption is that the purchase will be used as intended, and a comparison made at the shelf assumes a future meal plan that neither shopper has checked against what is already in the cupboard. The third is that price is the only attribute worth comparing, so a difference in how well the two keep, or how far they go in one dish, is treated as a matter of taste rather than as a difference in value. None of this makes the arithmetic wrong, and it is important to say so, because the useful correction is not to abandon the calculation but to know what question it answers. A per-kilo figure answers what a household buying a staple should ask, and that question is real. It is the wrong tool for a treat, a single meal, or anything bought to be used once, and recognising which of those a purchase is falls outside arithmetic entirely. The general lesson is that reducing two things to one number always gains something and always loses something, and the discipline is in naming what was discarded rather than in pretending nothing was.

questions.explanation: Administrative processes have more than one moment and the vocabulary names them, which is why two different verbs appear in the same exchange. 办理 is the citizen's side: it covers taking up a case, supplying what is needed, and following it, so a person who asks 怎样办理 is asking how to get into the process at all. 受理 is the office's side, and it is a specific moment rather than the whole business: the case has been formally received and entered, which is not the same as a decision and is not yet an outcome. A reader who keeps the two apart can navigate a process they know nothing about, because they can ask which stage they are at, and the answer will be a stage. The distractors each place the verbs wrongly. B is the reversal, and it is natural because a learner imagines the office as the active party in everything, which is exactly the assumption these two verbs exist to break. C notices a difference in wording and attributes it to tone, when the difference is in who is doing what. D gets the sequence rather than the roles wrong, and it is worth correcting because it produces a practical error: a person who believes 受理 means the process is finished will leave without the document.
questions.hint: Ask which of the two words has the citizen as its subject, and ask which office act 受理 names.

questions.topic: Steps in dealing with an office
questions.learningObjective: order the steps of an administrative process into a working sequence

questions.explanation: The workable order is the first, and the second step is the one that saves the trouble everybody expects to have. Asking what is required has to come first, because the list of documents is the one part of the process that is knowable in advance, and a person who assembles materials before asking will either bring something unnecessary or miss something necessary. Preparing them comes next, and copies matter because an office that keeps the original will say so and a person who has brought only the original has a problem that a return trip would have to solve. The submission step produces the piece of information that makes the rest of the process trackable, which is why the keyed sequence insists on a receipt for acceptance: without it there is nothing to produce when somebody asks whether the case was ever submitted, and the wait afterwards becomes indistinguishable from the case having been lost. The result comes last, and the last clause is the one that protects the person: a document is checked when it is collected, because a name written wrongly on a certificate is much harder to fix a year later than it is at the counter. The second option prepares before asking, which is the error the first step is designed to prevent. The third arrives at the counter with nothing, and the fourth begins waiting for a review that has not been sent.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: state the function of a referral in a health system
questions.stem: A clinic sends a patient to a hospital with a note naming the problem and the tests already done. What is that note for?

options.text: It tells the receiving doctor what has been established and what has not, so the hospital starts from the clinic's findings rather than repeating them
It transfers responsibility for the patient, so that the clinic is no longer answerable for the outcome of the case
options.misconception: reads a handover of information as a handover of liability, which is a legal question the note does not settle

options.text: It authorises the hospital to charge the patient, so the note is the document that creates the bill
options.misconception: gives a clinical document a financial function, which is handled by an entirely separate arrangement

options.text: It records that the patient refused treatment at the clinic, so the hospital knows the case was not accepted earlier
options.misconception: invents a refusal, when a referral is a request for a higher level of care and says nothing about consent at the first stage

questions.explanation: A referral is a summary for a reader who was not present, and the useful part of it is what it saves. Naming the problem and the tests already done tells the receiving doctor which questions have been answered and which have not, and that is worth a great deal in a system where a hospital would otherwise repeat an expensive investigation because nobody could tell it had been done. This is the same principle as the covering letter in a job application and the handover in a workplace, and it is worth learning as a general feature of institutions: work is handed from one specialist to another in a document, and the quality of the handover depends on whether the document says what has already been established. The distractors each attach a function the note does not have. B is the mistake that makes people reluctant to be referred, and it is worth addressing directly: the question of who is answerable is settled by the rules of the system and not by a piece of paper. C is a category error between a clinical document and a financial one. D invents a refusal, and a referral that recorded a refusal would be a complaint, not a referral.
questions.hint: Ask what the receiving doctor cannot know and what a note can tell them, and ask which questions it does not answer.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: The stages of the school system
questions.learningObjective: name the stages of the school system and the one that is compulsory
questions.stem: A student is told that a stage lasts six years, that it is free, and that every child must attend. Which stage is being described?

options.text: 小学, the six years of primary schooling that begin at about six and sit inside the compulsory years
初中, the three years of junior secondary schooling that follow the primary years
options.misconception: confuses the length of the stage, since three years rather than six describes the next one

options.text: 高中, the three years of upper secondary schooling that end with the national examination
options.misconception: puts a compulsory stage after the point where schooling stops being required

options.text: 幼儿园, the years before primary schooling that prepare a child for the first stage
options.misconception: moves the stage earlier, when the six years and the compulsory requirement belong together

questions.explanation: The description names primary schooling, and two features in it are worth separating because they are separate facts. Six years is a fact about the length of the stage. Free and compulsory is a fact about the legal obligation, and the two together locate the stage inside the nine years of compulsory schooling, which is six years of primary followed by three years of junior secondary. A learner who knows only the sequence will not be able to answer this, because the question is about the obligation rather than the order, and it is the obligation that varies: the years after the compulsory ones are free to attend in most places but are not required, which is a different status and one that matters a great deal to a family deciding whether a child can work. 高中 and 幼儿园 are both real stages and both are the wrong answer for a specific reason each, which is the pattern to notice in this kind of question: the distractors are not random, they are the neighbouring stages with one property changed. 幼儿园 is a preparatory year and in most places is not part of the compulsory years at all, so a statement that every child must attend it would be false.
questions.hint: Separate the two facts in the description: how long the stage lasts, and whether attendance is required.
