questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: The origin of a public holiday
questions.learningObjective: explain how a public holiday's origin is established from evidence
questions.stem: Explain in your own words why the date of a national holiday is evidence about its origin, and say what would have to be found to establish that a holiday commemorates a particular event.

answer.exemplar: A date is a piece of evidence rather than a decoration, because the day a country chose is usually the day something happened, and the choice is made after the event rather than before it. That is why the date is worth asking about and why it is never arbitrary. National Day falls on the first of October because that is when the founding of the People's Republic was proclaimed in 1949, and a holiday's date therefore points at a specific claim: this is the day, and here is what we are remembering. A second kind of holiday points the other way, since the first of May comes from an international workers' day and its date records a movement across several countries rather than a single event in one place. A learner who notices that the two kinds of holiday are different will already have the important analytical point, because the first kind of origin is a founding event and the second is a shared calendar. The test for whether a holiday really commemorates a particular event is worth stating separately, because the date alone is suggestive and not conclusive. Three kinds of evidence carry the weight. There has to be a contemporary record: a decree or a resolution issued at the time the holiday was created, naming what it was for. There has to be a public link between that record and the event: a date that matches, an organisation that already observed that day, or language in the announcement that names the occasion. And there has to been a continuity of observance, so that the claim is not one made in retrospect about a date that was kept for another reason. Where all three are present the claim is as well founded as historical claims of this kind get. Where the date coincides but no record names an event, the honest conclusion is that the coincidence is suggestive and the commemoration is unevidenced, and a learner who can say that is doing better than one who repeats a story they have heard. The general point is that holidays are documents as well as days off, and that reading them is a normal exercise in the same skills as reading any other public statement.

questions.explanation: The exemplar is marked correct for treating the date as a claim to be tested rather than a fact to be repeated, for distinguishing a founding event from a shared international calendar, and for naming three kinds of evidence rather than asserting that the date settles it. A response that says the date proves the origin has claimed more than the date can carry.
questions.hint: Ask what a date is evidence of, and what kind of document would have to exist for a commemoration claim to be established.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: order the school stages into the sequence a pupil passes through
questions.stem: Four school stages have been listed out of order by a class. Only one sequence is the order in which a pupil goes through them. Which sequence is it?

options.text: 小学 / 初中 / 高中 / 大学
初中 / 小学 / 高中 / 大学
小学 / 高中 / 初中 / 大学
小学 / 初中 / 大学 / 高中

questions.explanation: The order is the first one, and the way to hold it is as two pairs rather than as four items. The compulsory years are 小学 followed by 初中, six years and then three, and that block of nine comes first for every pupil. After it the routes do divide, which is the point worth adding since the simple sequence hides it: 高中 is the general upper secondary stage that most pupils take, while a vocational upper secondary route is a real alternative in many places, and both end with an examination whose result decides which higher education places a pupil can apply for. 大学 comes last because it is the point at which specialisation begins and the examinations that matter are the ones a pupil has already sat to get there. The second option puts the three-year stage before the six-year one. The third moves upper secondary ahead of junior secondary, which is a common error when a pupil is told about the examination first and the sequence is reconstructed from what was said. The fourth is the most natural-looking error of the four, because 大学 sounds like the summit of the system and a reader who has heard the word most often tends to place it early; it belongs last because it is where specialisation starts rather than where the sequence becomes shorter.
questions.hint: Group the stages into the compulsory block and what follows it, and check where specialisation begins.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: diagnose a claim about working life that the stated terms themselves contradict
questions.stem: Stage one: a notice says 我们是一家扁平化、没有级别的公司, and the same document lists four levels of title and says 报告给你的直属主管. Diagnose what in the notice contradicts the claim. Stage two: say what kind of claim the notice is making, and what a reader should ask before repeating it.

answer.exemplar: Stage one. The contradiction is not subtle and it does not need interpretation to see. 扁平化 and 没有级别 assert that the organisation has no hierarchy; four levels of title assert that it has one; and 报告给你的直属主管 names a person to whom a report is made, which is a relation that only exists between somebody above and somebody below. So the document does not merely fail to support the claim, it contradicts it three times over, using the same words in the same notice, and the reader has everything needed to reach that conclusion without leaving the page. What is worth noticing is the kind of word that produced the claim. 扁平化 is a borrowed term from the study of organisations, and a borrowed term arrives carrying the authority of the discipline it came from and none of its conditions. Flattening is a move away from layers, and a firm can flatten a great deal while keeping the layers that matter to a person's working life: who approves, who reviews, who is asked before a decision rather than told after it. So the honest diagnosis is that the claim is about a reduction in layers and has been stated as an absence of them, and that the statement is being made by a document which is itself arranged in layers. Stage two. The claim is a status claim, and status claims are the kind that are cheapest to make and hardest to check, because they cannot be true or false about a fact anyone will ever produce. A reader should ask what would have to be observed for the claim to be false, and if nothing could, the claim is not a description of anything. Here the answer is available: count the levels, and ask who signs off on leave, on pay, and on a decision to dismiss. An organisation with no levels has a way of showing that, and it is not a slogan. The second question is about who benefits from the claim being believed, because a status claim made in a notice read by staff is a claim being made to staff, and an employee who repeats it in a job interview has adopted a statement that the employer's own document contradicts. That is the practical harm, and it is why the exercise is worth doing rather than merely analysing.

questions.explanation: The exemplar is marked correct for finding the contradiction inside a single document rather than reaching for outside knowledge, for identifying the claim as a reduction of layers stated as an absence of them, and for the test of what would have to be observed for the claim to be false. A response that only notes the inconsistency has found the symptom and not the mechanism.
questions.hint: Ask which words in the notice do the contradicting, and what a reader would have to observe for the claim to be false.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: diagnose why a balanced household budget fails in practice and identify what it omits
questions.stem: Stage one: a family's budget adds up exactly, with no money left over and no reserve, and it fails anyway by the third month. Diagnose what a budget that balances can still be getting wrong. Stage two: say what the budget is missing, and why the missing part is the one that decides the year.

answer.exemplar: Stage one. A budget that balances exactly has proved that the income the family expected covers the spending it listed, and that is a statement about two lists rather than about a year. The diagnosis is therefore not that the arithmetic is wrong; the arithmetic is the one thing that is certainly right. What is wrong is the assumption underneath the lists, and there are three of them. The budget treats every figure as exact, so any price that moves, any income that arrives late, and any bill that is larger than forecast produces an immediate shortfall, and a plan with nothing spare has no way of meeting one. It treats the year as typical, so a household whose income is seasonal or whose spending is not has planned around an average that never actually arrives in any single month. And it leaves no reserve, which is the assumption that costs most, because a reserve is what converts an unexpected cost into an inconvenience rather than a crisis, and a household that has built none has not planned more tightly, it has planned more hopefully. The third month is worth attending to rather than treating as a detail, because it is the point at which the original figures have stopped matching reality, and a plan with no slack cannot absorb the first mismatch. Stage two. The missing part is the reserve, and its importance is not that it is prudent but that it changes what the rest of the plan can do. Every other figure in the budget is a forecast, and a forecast has to be wrong sometimes; the reserve is the only figure that is not forecasting anything, because it is the money that exists in order for a forecast to be wrong without consequence. It also has a second effect that is less often noticed, and it changes behaviour: a household with a reserve can decline an unexpected cost without taking on debt, and a household without one will borrow, which turns a cost into a commitment that lasts far longer than the cost. That is why the reserve decides the year rather than merely improving it. The general form of the lesson is that a plan has two jobs, to state what will probably happen and to survive what does not, and a budget that does the first perfectly and omits the second is not a tight budget. It is a precise one, and precision is not a substitute for slack.

questions.explanation: The exemplar is marked correct for saying the arithmetic is right and the assumptions are wrong, for treating the reserve as the only figure that is not a forecast, and for the point that a reserve changes behaviour because it makes refusing a debt possible. A response that says the family overspent has described the symptom the budget was always going to produce.
questions.hint: Ask which of the two jobs of a plan is being done, and which figure is the only one that is not a forecast.
